name: Paraiba
summary_text: Paraíba recorded 4 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, the same absolute count as Rio Grande do Norte. Against a population of ~4 million this yields approximately 1.0 per million per year—well above the national rate of ~0.38/million and among the highest in the federation. The state is part of the Northeast bloc that absorbed 38 of 80 national killings (47.5%) in 2025. The per-capita rate places Paraíba roughly 0.09 below the national 0.71. Compared with Alagoas (0.68), which had 2 killings in a similar population (~3.3 M, rate ~0.61/million), Paraíba's absolute count is double and its rate higher, reflecting the broader Northeast concentration on a smaller denominator. No Paraíba-specific legal or ordinance evidence was found; the deviation is driven entirely by the violence dataset. The victim profile—young, Black, poor, Northeastern—concentrates risk on individuals who present visibly in public space.

sources.title: Brasil lidera ranking mundial de assassinatos de pessoas trans | SBT News
sources.claim_summary: SBT News report (26 Jan 2026) on the 9th edition of the ANTRA dossier: Brazil recorded 80 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, down 34% on 2024, still the world's highest; state counts for 2025 - Ceará and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7, Goiás/Maranhão/Pará 5, Paraíba, Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte and São Paulo 4 each, Mato Grosso and Rio de Janeiro 3, Alagoas, Distrito Federal, Espírito Santo and Mato Grosso do Sul 2; 1,261 killings 2017-2025 (~140/yr); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, 70% Black, 67.5% committed outside state capitals.

sources.title: Brasil é o país que mais mata pessoas trans e travestis, aponta dossiê | CNN Brasil
sources.claim_summary: CNN Brasil dossier summary: Brazil is 'the country that kills most trans people and travestis'; victim profile young, Black, poor and Northeastern, with life expectancy of about 35; killings mostly in public places, at night, with exceptional cruelty, and routinely mis-recorded by authorities; regional panorama for 2024: São Paulo 16, Minas Gerais 12, Ceará 11, Rio de Janeiro 10, Bahia/Mato Grosso/Pernambuco 8 each, Alagoas 6.
